newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma chairman says Chubais must be sacked.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma chairman says Chubais must be sacked.

text.p: The communist head of Russia's lower house of parliament on Wednesday called on President Boris Yeltsin to sack chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, saying he would not work with him in a new consultative body.

Gennady Seleznyov, chairman of the State Duma, said he protested against Chubais because of the appointment on Tuesday of businessman Boris Berezovsky as deputy secretary of Yeltsin's policy-making Security Council.
Seleznyov said Chubais, who has had a big influence over Kremlin affairs while Yeltsin prepares for heart surgery, must have been behind Berezovsky's appointment.

Berezovsky, a controversial businessman, was assigned the post as part of a reorganisation of the Security Council following the sacking of its outspoken former secretary Alexander Lebed, ousted for his overt presidential ambitions.
The row could jeopardise efforts to smooth over a power struggle which has broken out with Yeltsin's absence from public life with heart problems since he was re-elected in July.
Chubais, who presided over Russia's privatisation programme from 1992 to 1996, has been accused of controlling access to Yeltsin and having undue influence over affairs of state.

"I insist on the immediate dismissal of the president's head of administration, Anatoly Chubais. I do not doubt that I am expressing the opinion of an absolute majority of Russian citizens," Seleznyov said in a statement.

Berezovsky, 50, has business interests ranging from car dealerships to television. Seleznyov said he had used his position on the board of the biggest state television channel to stage an "anti-Russian information coup".
He did not explain what he meant, but communists complained during this year's presidential election campaign of heavy media bias against them.

Berezovsky was not immediately available for comment on the allegations. He earlier told Itar-Tass news agency his sphere of activity in the council had not been laid down but would be discussed on Wednesday.
He underlined the importance of economic change to Russia's security and added: "I think my experience in this respect will be useful for the further progress of economic reforms in Russia."

The Security Council, headed by Yeltsin, groups senior government ministers, including those of defence and the interior, and officials of the Federal Security Service (FSB), successor organisation of the Soviet-era KGB.
Military commander Leonid Mayorov was appointed along with Berezovsky on Tuesday as a deputy to Ivan Rybkin, Lebed's successor as council secretary.
Mayorov, 41, who has commanded troops in northwest Russia since 1992, told Tass he would look after the military industrial complex and a peace settlement for rebel Chechnya.

Yeltsin sacked Lebed, a reserve general with his sights on the presidency, this month. Rybkin is a moderate communist with a proven track record of loyalty to the president. wly-formed consultative council -- aimed at increasing cooperation between the executive and the legislature -- was due to hold its first meeting this Friday.
It consists of a "permanent four" -- Seleznyov, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Chubais and Yegor Stroyev -- the chairman of the Federation Council upper chamber.
